extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, prospective members, students, and academics in India
extracted.subtask_description: Informational guidance from the Public Relations Society of India about its purpose, membership classes and processes, governance, activities, recognition, and the observance of National Public Relations Day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Society / Professional recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Relations Society of India (PRSI) ... established in 1958 to promote the recognition of public relations as a profession and to formulate and interpret to the public the objectives and the potentialities of public relations as a strategic management function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains PRSI's founding mission: elevate PR from publicity/press-agentry/information to a recognized profession and to communicate PR's objectives and strategic management role to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management / Governance structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The management of the Public Relations society of India is vested in the National Council, consisting of representatives elected by all the regional chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance is centralized in a National Council whose members are elected by regional chapters, implying chapter-level representation and collective decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility and admission process
rubrics_metrics.description: The membership of the society is open to any person and also to any firm, body corporate or association of persons. Such membership take effect on admission and classification at the discretion of the National Council. Each application for membership is forwarded by the Regional Chapter to the National Council for consideration with their recommendations regarding acceptance and classification, and forward the same to the Secretary-General for consideration of the National Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is broadly open (individuals and organizations). Admission and classification are discretionary decisions of the National Council, with regional chapters responsible for forwarding applications with recommendations to the Secretary-General/National Council. (Note: paragraph is repeated verbatim on the page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of membership
rubrics_metrics.description: There are following classes of members : Members; Life Members; Associate Members; Honorary Members; and Student Members
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the membership categories PRSI recognises; selection of appropriate class likely governed by council procedures (not detailed on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional approach / shift from publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The theme of the conference was ‘Professional Approach’. This was a very significant public relations meet in our country, when a professional approach was given to public relations ( a change from publicity, press a gentry, information) besides adopting a Code of Ethics for PR profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the standard that PR practice should be professional (distinct from mere publicity or press-agentry) and aligned with an adopted Code of Ethics; historically linked to the First All India Public Relations Conference (April 21, 1968).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of a Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides adopting a Code of Ethics for PR profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that PRSI adopted an ethical code as part of its professionalisation efforts; while the page does not reproduce the Code, it signals ethical standards are a core expectation for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Regional Chapters / Professional development activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regional Chapters of the society regularly organize seminars, lectures and discussions on various facets of public relations. In order to promote professional training, the chapters run, with the collaboration of universities and colleges, professional programme on public relations for students of management, PR, advertising, mass communication and journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters are expected to deliver continuing education and outreach—seminars, lectures, discussions, and academic collaborations—to promote professional training for students and practitioners across related disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and international affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: The society is recognized as the national PR organization by the International Public Relations Association, and is one of the founder members of the Global Alliance of Public Relations and Communications Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSI's recognition by international bodies establishes it as the national representative for India in global PR forums and networks, implying adherence to international professional norms and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Public Relations Day (purpose and observance)
rubrics_metrics.description: April 21, is ... the National public Relations Day ... celebrated on this day all over the country since 1986. The objective behind designating April 21 as National Public Relations Day is to focus attention on public relations function and public relations professionals in India who have an increasingly important role in the development of the country. Specific theme for the day is identified to organise events to highlight the issues selected in the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual observance is used to highlight PR's role and to organise theme-based events; origin tied to First All India Public Relations Conference (April 21, 1968). Encourages theme selection and events to draw attention to contemporary PR issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical continuity and major events
rubrics_metrics.description: Since then, PRSI had 26 All India PR conferences including the 9th PR World Congress in Bombay in 1982 and the first Asia Pacific PR Meet in Kolkata during January, 1998 and International Public Relations Conference at Bangalore in 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents PRSI's historical activity and participation in major conferences, suggesting an expectation of sustained national and international engagement as part of organisational practice.
